newsitem.title: CHINA: China H1 budget surplus 38.85 billion yuan.
newsitem.headline: China H1 budget surplus 38.85 billion yuan.

text.p: China saw a budget surplus of 38.85 billion yuan ($4.7 billion) in the first six months of 1997 fuelled by an increase in the stamp tax on stock trading and reduced payments of export tax rebates, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

National revenue, excluding revenue from state debt, reached 390.108 billion yuan in the first half of the year, an increase of 29.9 percent from the year-ago period, Xinhua quoted Minister of Finance Liu Zhongli as saying.
National expenditures were 351.26 billion yuan in the first six months, a year-on-year rise of 21.1 percent, Liu was quoted as telling a conference on government finance.

An increase in May in the stamp tax on securities trading to 0.5 percent from 0.3 percent and reductions in the amount of tax rebates paid to exporters had helped to boost first half revenue, Liu said.

But problems such as tax evasion by enterprises and too-high expenditures by some regions were obstacles in implementing the 1997 national budget, with its goal of bringing the deficit down to 56 billion yuan, he said.
"As far as revenue is concerned, the number of enterprises that owe taxes is increasing, mainly in owing value-added and commercial taxes," Xinhua quoted him as saying.
"Although growth in national fiscal expenditures was lower than growth in revenue, expenditures in some places has risen sharply," he said without elaborating.
Tax authorities should step up management and supervision of tax collection and strike out at tax evaders and officials who gave out unauthorised tax breaks, he said.
China would trim supplementary spending in the second half of the year except for special situations such as disaster relief and grain purchasing subsidies, he said but gave no further details.
China recorded a budget surplus of 41.532 billion yuan in the first five months of this year, earlier figures showed.
Beijing has said it expects a budget deficit of about 56 billion yuan this year, down from nearly 61 billion yuan in 1996.
